raw:
I had to hand back before the final acceptance run finished, so this fix round has no evidence and returns `failed`. The code fixes for B1–B3 are all committed on feature/US-02-03 (not pushed). The run on head 33390cd was still going in the background when I was told to stop, so I have not collected it and have no results from it.

What the CI failure actually was (from run 38781983403's JUnit and log):
- **TC-02-06 is a real layout bug.** On the 320 × 640 dp CI screen the 5+ entry fell below the bottom edge.
- **TC-03-07, TC-02-12 and TC-03-08 failed because the emulator dropped off adb**, not because of the app. TC-03-07 died with "Device server died during 'viewHierarchy'"; TC-02-12 (44 ms) and TC-03-08 (32 ms) failed with "Unknown error" after that. Earlier, TC-03-01's app launch took 363 s instead of the usual ~7 s, so the emulator was already struggling. The emulator was still alive at the end of the job (`emu kill` answered OK), so it was a temporary drop, not a crash.
- **Every later group was reported blocked within about one second**, including TC-02-13 (deck-state) and TC-02-11 (de-DE). That is why they were never executed.

What I did with the two commits the earlier session left:
- **c37f960 (layout fix, DEC-64): kept.** DEC-64 was properly reserved through `og-delivery dec next`: it is in `.git/og-delivery/decs.json` for US-02-03, at 2026-10-15T18:45:21Z, with the same title.
- **6d2b843 (blocked messages name a lost device, TC-02-13 named in the deck-state group): kept.**
- **The earlier session's local run on 6d2b843** (test-runs/2026-10-15_204639) ran with the emulator set to 320x640 at density 160, like CI. TC-02-06, TC-02-12, TC-02-13, TC-03-07 and TC-03-08 all passed, along with the other pl and deck-state flows and TC-03-11..14. It was cut off at TC-03-15, so TC-02-08, TC-02-09 and TC-02-11 never ran, and it was never collected (no run.json). It is not on the current head.

What I added:
- **33390cd** adds a `device_back` step to `scripts/test-acceptance.sh`. Before each group of flows after the Polish one, it waits up to 3 minutes for the device to come back, waits for boot to complete and roots it again. The remaining groups then run instead of all being blocked at once.
  - It re-runs nothing: a flow that failed while the device was gone stays failed.
  - It does not wait on an image that cannot be rooted.
  - I checked it by hand on the local emulator: after `adb unroot`, it rooted the device again.
- The gates passed on 33390cd: format, lint, types and unit tests (37 suites, 250 tests).

What is still needed: the CI emulator is fragile, and `device_back` lets the later groups run but does not fix that. Lowering its load would mean changing `.github/workflows/acceptance.yml` (for example its RAM size), which is not mine to change. A green result therefore depends on a CI run on the pushed head where the emulator stays up.
